line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
reading: You feel overthinking and get angry when someone stops you from having good food. Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong, and that holding it feels like holding the wind. When your thoughts race like this, you are in the same company as the finest archer. Rest your attention on the next bite of food in front of you.

line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
reading: You wake at 2 a.m. with the same meeting replaying. Arjuna, the finest archer, told Krishna that the mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong, as hard to hold as the wind. Your mind tonight is doing exactly what he named. Rest on the fact that this restlessness is not yours alone to fix.

line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
reading: Your exam results are coming out on Friday, and the anxiety is making it hard to eat. Krishna tells Arjuna that your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. You can care for your preparation today and take one small bite, knowing the outcome is not yours to hold.

line: "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name."
reading: The house is quiet now that your son has moved to Canada. Krishna, far from Mathura, tells his mother Yashoda, "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name." In your quiet home today, no one may call you by the name you once knew in a fuller house. Let the silence hold that missing name.

line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
reading: Your brother took your share of the house, and that injustice still burns. Krishna tells Narada that harsh words from relatives keep churning the heart like a fire-stick, day after day. You do not have to smooth this over; you can simply let the fire he lit keep burning, and sit with that heat today.

line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
reading: You feel shaken after your layoff. The Bhagavad Gita opens with Arjuna telling Krishna that his limbs give way, his mouth is parched, and his body trembles. Your three months of savings may feel like a thin buffer against that same raw uncertainty, yet the verse names the fear plainly without asking you to fix it today.

line: Quiet, you're dull; talkative, a show-off; patient, weak. Serving a boss is harder than yoga.
reading: You feel hurt because your team lead presented your analysis to the director as his own. Bhartrihari warns that serving a boss is harder than yoga, because keeping quiet makes you dull, and speaking up makes you a show-off. Today, your work itself was real, even if the credit was not; let that truth remain with you when you close your laptop tonight.

line: What hurt most was not the news, but that he didn't tell me himself.
reading: You carry the hurt of words that find fault with everything you do, even how you cook. Rama says only one sorrow burns his heart: that the king did not tell him himself about Bharata's coronation. Like his, your pain sits in the silence behind the harshness, not in the act itself. You can sit with that unshared truth today, letting it be what it is.

line: Speaking of pain lightens it. But whom can I tell? No one knows this ache.
reading: You keep looking at old photos after your breakup. Ram says that telling one's grief lightens it a little, but asks whom he can tell since no one knows this ache. That same ache is alive in you today when you open those pictures. Let your heart hold the truth of what you shared, even if no one else sees it.

line: "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name."
reading: You are far from your father in Kanpur while stuck in Toronto. Krishna tells his mother Yashoda, "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name," missing the warmth of home. Like him, you may feel unseen in this distant city. Hold on to the name your father still uses for you, and let that memory ground you today.

line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
reading: With twins at six months, your nights have barely rested. Bhasa says the mind caught in endless lists—'done this, doing this, must do that'—never finds a moment's pause. Your own to-dos may feel like those great waves, carrying you while worry dances in the depths. Notice the exact moment today when one small task ends and the next begins, and let the mind rest there for a breath.

line: The mind pounces on a task like a bird on food, then drops it like a bored child's toy.
reading: Your mind keeps landing on watching reels and then letting go, just as Rama told the sages it pounces on a task like a bird on food and drops it like a bored child's toy. This same restlessness can show up while you sit down to write your thesis. Today, when you open your notes, notice the pull toward the next reel and simply place one sentence on the page before you decide to stay or go.

line: Every good quality I take up, craving gnaws through, like a mouse chewing a string.
reading: You feel restless, and late at night you keep ordering things online. The Maha Upanishad has Nidagha say that craving gnaws through every good quality, like a mouse chewing a string. That same quiet gnawing might be at work in your screen-lit hours, slowly chewing through whatever steadiness you try to build. Notice the next item arriving, and the string it pulls.

line: What is a kingdom to me, or pleasure? Who am I, and what is all this for?
reading: You reached the VP title at 38 and now feel hollow inside. Young Rama asks, 'What is a kingdom to me, or pleasure? Who am I, and what is all this for?' Your title is real, yet it does not answer who you are beneath it. Let that question sit with you today as you walk into work.

line: I have no devotion, no wisdom, no steady love. But he loves the one who has nowhere else to go.
reading: You feel everyone in your new role seems smarter than you, and you are waiting to be found out. Sutikshna says he has no wisdom or steady love, yet the compassionate one loves the one who has nowhere else to go. In your team today, you might simply sit with that doubt without hiding it, knowing you do not need another refuge.

line: I started this with determination, and determination will carry me to the end.
reading: You are training for your first marathon in March. Savitri tells her father-in-law, 'I started this with determination, and determination will carry me to the end.' That same resolve can steady you on the long miles ahead, carrying the training you began in January through to the finish line.

line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
reading: You want to understand what the Gita actually says. Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of good people worship him: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise. Your curiosity places you among those welcomed here. Pick up the text and read the next chapter where Krishna begins to explain.

line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
reading: Your mother recovered from her surgery, and you feel thankful. Bhartrihari asks what generous austerity earned him this freedom, simple food, good company, and a mind that stirs only gently. You can sit with that same calm today, letting the quiet gratitude for her healing simply rest in your chest.

line: The self was never born and never dies. It is not killed when the body is.
reading: You are carrying the loss of your dad since March, and the emptiness you feel is real. Krishna tells Arjuna that the self was never born and never dies; it is not slain when the body is slain. That means the core of who your dad was still exists beyond his passing, sitting quietly beside your grief today.

line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
reading: You are torn between a startup offer and an MNC, with a Friday deadline. Arjuna tells Krishna that his nature is stricken by weakness and his mind is confused about what is right, asking plainly what is best. Today, your own confusion about this choice is real. You can bring that same honesty to the decision, simply stating, 'I do not know what is best, teach me.'

line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
reading: Comparison is mostly a voice that pushes you down. Krishna says you can be your own friend or your own enemy, and asks you to lift yourself up. Start by noticing which one you've been lately.

line: Why do I do the wrong thing even when I don't want to, as if something forces me?
reading: You carry the weight of a lie told to your wife about money, and now it has come out. Krishna hears Arjuna ask what drives a person to do wrong even against their will, as if forced by something outside themselves. That question may sit with you today, naming the force that moved you then without excusing the breach. You can look your wife in the eye and speak the remaining truth about what is still hidden.

line: Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, too overwhelmed to go on.
reading: After your third startup failed, you feel close to giving up. Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that Arjuna put down his bow and sat in his chariot, his mind overwhelmed by grief. Like Arjuna, you can lay down the weight of this loss and simply sit with it today. Your bow rests on the seat beside you.

line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
reading: You are caught between a big work deadline and the kids' board exams this week, feeling wound tight. Krishna tells Arjuna that contact with the world brings heat and cold, pleasure and pain that come and go, so bear them patiently. Right now, that means letting the pressure move through you until it passes, and noticing one slow breath before you turn to the next task.

line: Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.
reading: You are scared the new director role will change who you are. Krishna tells Arjuna that whatever a respected person does, others copy, and the standard they set is the one the world follows. Your team and juniors are already watching how you step into this. Let your daily choices at work quietly show them who you remain.

line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
reading: You are starting your first job in Bangalore next week, and hope is already with you. Lakshman tells Ram that enthusiasm is powerful, and for the one who has it, nothing is out of reach. Let that steadiness meet your first commute and first desk. Carry it into the city this week.

line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of good people worship him—those in distress, those seeking knowledge, those seeking wealth, and the wise. You want to feel Krishna close during your morning puja. In that quiet time, you already belong among those who turn to the divine with love.

line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
reading: You want to go deeper after feeling calm on your retreat. Krishna tells Arjuna that the one who is happy within, at ease within, and lit from within finds lasting freedom. That inner light can stay with you today, even as you return to work.

line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
reading: You snapped at your team today and they went quiet. Krishna tells Arjuna that when a person dwells on objects, attachment is born, and from attachment comes desire, which then turns into anger. That quiet in the room today is the wall meeting a wanting that had been building while your mind kept dwelling on something. Notice the pause before the next meeting, and let your attention rest there.

line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
reading: You trusted your business partner with money, and he cheated you. Krishna says his relatives' harsh words keep burning him day after day. You can carry that same fire-stick anger without letting it define your next move today.

line: I have someone who is mine, and still I feel like a person with no one at all.
reading: You feel alone even while sharing a home. Sita told Ram, 'I have someone who is mine, and still I feel like a person with no one at all.' That quiet distance beside you can echo this same ache today. Notice the one person who remains yours, and let that truth sit with you.

line: Day again, night again, the same tasks again, over and over. A thinking person feels mocked by it.
reading: Ten years of 14 hour days have left you completely burnt out. Bali, a king who has ruled for ages, looks out his window and says, "Again day, again night, again the same chain of tasks. Again and again: to a thinking person, I feel, this is a mockery." That same cycle you have lived through can feel like a mockery to your thinking mind today. Rest your eyes on the window before you, and simply notice the day ending.

line: "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name."
reading: Caring for your mother with dementia alone leaves you feeling restless. Krishna, far from home in Mathura, tells his mother Yashoda, "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name." In your own home, the weight of the days may make you feel unseen beyond your caregiving role. Notice the quiet space around your own name today, and let it rest there.

line: What hurt most was not the news, but that he didn't tell me himself.
reading: You feel the sting of being blamed at home. Rama says his heart burns because his father did not tell him the truth himself. That silence still hurts him even after he accepts everything else. Today, that same ache of unspoken blame can sit heavy in your chest.

line: My heart feels heavy as stone, but I don't cry, because of what people would think.
reading: It sounds like you're carrying something very heavy right now.

line: My heart feels heavy as stone, but I don't cry, because of what people would think.
reading: It sounds like you're carrying something very heavy right now.

line: I live here like the tongue among the teeth.
reading: It sounds like home doesn't feel safe right now.

line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
reading: Your mind feels restless and stubborn right now. Arjuna, the greatest archer of his time, told Krishna that holding his mind is as hard as holding the wind. Like him, you are not failing when thoughts race; your mind simply has its own force today.

line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that contact between the senses and their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain, which come and go and do not last. For you today, this means the anxious pressure you carry while studying is also passing. Notice the deadline or the hard week as it touches you, and let it move on.

line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
reading: You carry a heavy load of care and feel anxious. Krishna tells Arjuna that contact with the world brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain, which come and go and do not last. You can bear this shifting tide of worry as it passes, noticing the next breath in your own chest.

line: See me in everything and everything in me, and I never lose you, nor you me.
reading: You feel lonely in this retired season. Krishna tells Arjuna, See me in everything and everything in me, and I never lose you, nor you me. When the world outside feels quiet, this presence stays close, never slipping away, and you stay close to it too. You might notice this steadiness in the morning light on your balcony.

line: What hurt most was not the news, but that he didn't tell me himself.
reading: You carry a hurt that burns even when other things settle. Rama says only one sorrow still burns his heart: that the king did not tell him himself about Bharata's coronation. Today, that same ache of being left out of the truth can sit heavy in your home. You might find quiet relief in naming one specific silence that still stings, and letting it rest there.

line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
reading: You carry anger right now. Krishna tells Arjuna that when a person dwells on objects, attachment is born, then desire, and from desire comes anger. Your frustration today may be the final spark of a fire that has been building while you kept returning to what blocked you. Notice the moment your mind fixes on that obstacle, before the heat rises.

line: He no longer laughs at jokes, enjoys pleasures, or stays with his work. He just goes quiet.
reading: You feel empty. The Yoga Vasishtha describes how Rama no longer laughs at jokes, enjoys pleasures, or stays with his work, and just keeps silent. In your working life, that same quiet withdrawal can be a true pause rather than a failure. Let this silence be the quiet space you sit in today.

line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
reading: You feel stuck and unable to get started. Arjuna asks Krishna what happens to someone who believes and tries, yet slips before reaching the end. This speaks to you today by naming the fear behind your pause: trying and falling short is still a real path, not a dead end. Rest in the question itself, and let your next small step be simply showing up again.

line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
reading: You feel grateful in this retired stage of life. The poet Bhartrihari asks what generous austerity earned this freedom to wander at will, simple food without humiliation, noble company, and learning whose only fruit is calm. Your mind stirs gently even when it looks outward for long. You can rest in the simple food you eat today and the calm it brings.

line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
reading: Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of good people worship him: those in distress, those seeking wealth, those seeking knowledge, and the wise. Your curiosity places you among these welcome seekers. Let this verse sit with you today as you open your book.

line: Each work has to pass through these stages — ridicule, opposition, and then acceptance.
reading: You feel determined right now. Swami Vivekananda wrote that each work has to pass through stages of ridicule, opposition, and then acceptance. That path speaks to you today as you study, because your resolve may meet resistance before it finds its place. Keep your focus on the work itself.

line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
reading: You feel hopeful about what lies ahead. Lakshman tells Ram that enthusiasm is powerful and there is no strength greater than it. For the one who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach. Let that truth ground you today as you step into this new beginning, trusting the energy already within you to carry you forward.

line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
reading: You feel restless right now. The verse says, 'Done this, doing this, must do that'—the mind caught in endless lists never gets a moment's rest. Your own days of raising kids can feel like that same tangled net. Notice the next breath you take after putting a toy away; that pause is the mind resting, even for a second.

line: Why do I do the wrong thing even when I don't want to, as if something forces me?
reading: You carry guilt about past mistakes while caring for your parents. Arjuna asks Krishna why a person does wrong even against their will, as if forced by something stronger. This verse names the very weight you feel today, pointing to a force beyond your control rather than your own failing. Rest in that distinction when the guilt returns tonight.

line: Like a poor man before the wishing tree, we hesitate to ask for what we really want.
reading: You feel uneasy inside. Manu tells Vishnu that even standing before the wish-fulfilling tree, a poor man still hesitates to ask for what he truly wants, not knowing its power, and doubt rises in his heart. This mirrors your own pause today: the power to ask for what you want is already there, so let your next step simply be naming one thing you actually want.

line: Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.
reading: You feel inspired as you run your own thing. Krishna tells Arjuna that whatever a respected person does, others copy, and the standard they set is the one people follow. This speaks to you today because your team and younger peers look to how you carry your success. Let your grounded actions today be the quiet standard they quietly mirror.

line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
reading: You feel peaceful now. Krishna says the one whose happiness, delight and light are all within becomes one with Brahman and reaches its peace. This points to a joy that does not wait on outside events. Your inner light already carries this freedom today.

line: Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, too overwhelmed to go on.
reading: You feel lost right now. Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, his mind overwhelmed by grief. Like Arjuna, you can set down what you carry and simply sit. Rest in that stillness today, letting your bow rest beside you.
